gen_risks.description: Insufficient funding for schools to deliver free breakfast clubs, potentially impacting programme effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Regular review of funding model and allocation, with adjustments as needed to ensure sufficient support for schools.
gen_risks.evidence: Financial case: funding approach and costs.

gen_risks.description: Difficulty in recruiting and retaining skilled staff to deliver free breakfast clubs, affecting programme quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Development of training and support programs for staff, and exploration of incentives to attract and retain qualified personnel.

gen_risks.description: Inequitable access to free breakfast clubs due to variations in school resources and capacity, potentially exacerbating existing inequalities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Targeted support for disadvantaged schools, and monitoring of programme accessibility and equity.
gen_risks.evidence: Strategic case: food insecurity and childcare costs.

gen_risks.description: Delays or challenges in implementing the customer relationship management system, hindering school support and programme efficiency.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritized development and testing of the system, with contingency planning for potential delays or issues.
gen_risks.evidence: Commercial case: customer relationship management system.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient engagement and participation from schools, potentially limiting programme reach and impact.
gen_risks.mitigation: Proactive outreach and communication with schools, and incentives for participation and engagement.
gen_risks.evidence: Commercial case: school recruitment and participation.

gen_risks.description: Difficulty in meeting the legislative requirements and timelines for implementing free breakfast clubs, potentially leading to non-compliance or delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Close collaboration with relevant authorities and stakeholders, and proactive planning to ensure compliance with legislative requirements.
gen_risks.evidence: Strategic case: Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate infrastructure and resources in schools to support free breakfast clubs, potentially impacting programme quality and safety.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assessment of school infrastructure and resources, with targeted support and investment to address gaps and needs.

gen_risks.description: Challenges in collecting and analyzing data on programme outcomes and impact, potentially limiting evaluation and improvement efforts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Development of a robust data collection and analysis system, with regular review and refinement to ensure data quality and utility.
gen_risks.evidence: Evaluation plan: data collection and analysis.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient consideration of the needs and perspectives of parents and carers, potentially leading to inadequate programme design and delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Proactive engagement with parents and carers, and incorporation of their feedback and perspectives into programme design and delivery.
gen_risks.evidence: Evaluation plan: parent and school perspectives.

gen_risks.description: Difficulty in sustaining programme funding and support over time, potentially leading to reduced programme effectiveness and impact.
gen_risks.mitigation: Development of a long-term funding strategy, and exploration of opportunities for sustainable funding and support.
gen_risks.evidence: Financial case: funding approach and costs.

gt_risks.description: Lower value for money compared to the 'do minimum' option in year 1, due to the shorter funding period available for the preferred option's new cohorts of schools.
Delivery risks around staffing and food costs for schools newly onboarded to the free breakfast clubs programme.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated through early adopter (EA) scheme insights and support funding.

gt_risks.description: Uncertainty in the labour-market benefits (parental workforce participation gains) the programme is expected to deliver.
gt_risks.mitigation: Addressed through conservative assumptions in the economic modelling.
